text: and good morning everyone and welcome to our board meeting of april 11th 2023 and as we always do at the beginning of our meeting we are going to recognize anyone in our community that we would like to keep in our thoughts and prayers immediately following that we are going to stand for a moment of silence and then the pledge of allegiance and then we begin the work part of our meeting today and before we do that i'll ask my colleagues if they have anyone they would like to remember Let me just start with one, and that is Mike Tamelo.

Some people may know Mike Tamelo. Our public safety family is mourning his loss. He was a battalion chief who passed away on March 10th. Although he retired from the Fairfax County Fire Department in 2003, Battalion Chief Tamelo helped develop our elite urban search and rescue program in Fairfax County.

And he has led Virginia Task Force One on many missions, including his first mission to the earthquake in Armenia, as well as earthquakes in the Philippines, Turkey, Taiwan, and Iran. Many of us remember all of those well.

He was also part of the team that responded to the Oklahoma City bombing, U.S. Embassy bombing in Kenya, and, of course, to the Pentagon on 9-11. Battalion Chief Tamelo's death comes after being diagnosed with a work-related lung cancer back in 2020 and serves as a reminder of the risk that our firefighters take every day in serving our community.

I'd like to take this opportunity, of course, to thank IAFF for their efforts in getting members screened for early detection of potential health issues given the variety of chemicals and carcinogens that our Fire and Rescue Department come into contact with regularly.

And so if we could keep Mike Tamelo, our Fire and Rescue Department, our public safety family, in our thoughts and prayers, it would be appreciated. With that, we'll recognize other board members. Let me start with Supervisor Gross to be followed by Supervisor Faust.

Thank you, Mr. Chairman. One of the most iconic institutions in Fairfax County and Hunter Mill District is the VNAN. I think most of us are familiar with that place, especially if you like chili dogs and maybe certain beverages. For four decades, Molly Bass Abraham owned and operated the Vienna Inn with her late husband, Meyer.
So, but after living a full life, Molly passed away on March 25 at age 96. Molly was born in Baltimore on June 2, 1926, and moved to Alexandria with her newlywed husband, Meyer Abraham, in 1949.

Meyer preceded Molly in death in November 1999. The Abrahams bought the Vienna Inn, which was known at the time as Freddy's, in 1960, and made it an integral part of the Vienna community until selling it in 1999. In addition to the restaurant, Molly's passions were many, and some folks may not realize some of these.

From the days of racial segregation to the Equal Rights Amendment, Molly was on the front lines. She was instrumental in founding the Alexandria chapter of the National Organization for Women and served as the Virginia State Coordinator for that organization. She was chair of the Commission for Women for two terms, advocating equal pay and retirement benefits.

After selling the VNN, she worked for Common Cause, and in 2011, Molly was named a living legend in acknowledgement of her significant contributions to the quality of life in Alexandria. She was also active with PTAs and school functions while raising her three children, so a very life well-lived, and our condolences to her family, including several grandchildren and great-grandchildren.
